references.text: God blessed Noah and his sons and said to them: "Be fruitful and multiply and fill the earth!" This is the immediate context for 9:7 and contains almost identical wording, framing God's command to Noah and his descendants.
God blessed them and said to them: "Be fruitful and multiply, fill the earth and subdue it!" God's original command to humanity to be fruitful and multiply, repeated after the flood.

God blessed them and said: "Be fruitful and multiply and fill the waters in the sea, and let birds multiply on the earth!" The first occurrence of the command to 'be fruitful and multiply', given to creatures of the sea and birds.

All the animals that are with you, of all flesh, both birds, livestock and all creeping things that creep on the earth, you shall bring out with you, and they shall swarm on the earth and be fruitful and multiply on the earth. God's command that animals should be fruitful and multiply on the earth after the flood, parallel to the command given to humans.

God said to him: "I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply! A nation, yes, a company of nations shall come from you, and kings shall issue from your loins." God's promise to Jacob of fruitfulness and many descendants, an echo of the original command to humanity.

He blesses them so that they become very numerous, and He does not let their livestock become small. God's blessing with fruitfulness and abundance, reflecting the theme of being fruitful and multiplying.

From one man He has made all nations, so that they dwell over the whole surface of the earth. The common origin and spread of humanity across the earth as a fulfillment of the command to fill the earth.
Connection between the general calling to humanity and the specific covenant promise to become a multitude of nations.
Thematic parallel where numerous offspring are presented as a central element in God's blessing.
Theological contrast between God's blessing to fill the earth and His judgment to scatter the people.
Prophetic restoration of Israel as a new creation, directly parallel to the restoration after the flood.
Continuity in God's covenant promise of fruitfulness and nation-building from Noah to Jacob.
Prophetic use of the creation and flood motifs to describe future restoration and expansion.
Continuity in the covenant promise to become a multitude of nations from Noah to Joseph.
Historical fulfillment of God's plan to let His people 'spread out' in the promised land.
Covenant obligation that resumes and confirms God's promise of fertility from the flood.
